summary: Sullivan County tower the Forest Lookouts page ties to a December 1913 newspaper report; both sources list it as removed. No site description found.

facts.status_note: Both sources list the tower as removed; neither gives a removal date.
facts.design: Timber tower on a high peak, anchored twelve feet below ground (1913 newspaper description)

events.note: Tennessean report dated 1913-12-09 says the government had completed the first lookout tower in the White Top area near Bristol; the Forest Lookouts page places it at Whitetop Knobs

evidence.supports: 1913 report: government completed first lookout tower in the White Top area near Bristol
evidence.quote: The government has completed the first lookout tower for fire prevention in the Appalachian Forest reserve, in the White Top area near Bristol.

evidence.supports: page names the site Whitetop Knobs
tower on a high peak; view into North Carolina, Virginia and Tennessee
evidence.quote: The tower is situated on a high peak and rises to such a height that a person familiar with the country can locate a fire in the mountains in North Carolina, Virginia or Tennessee, by means of a field glass.

evidence.supports: towers built of large timbers, anchored twelve feet underground
evidence.quote: The towers are built of huge timbers and anchored twelve feet under ground.

evidence.supports: several more towers planned and linked by telephone
evidence.quote: Several of these towers will be erected and they will be connected by telephones to be installed at once.

evidence.supports: page marks the tower as removed
tnlandforms marks Whitetop Knobs as removed

sources.title: TN lookout tower: SUT002 Whitetop Knobs

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1913 report says 'White Top area near Bristol' and does not name Whitetop Knobs. The Forest Lookouts page makes that identification; the story attributes it to the page rather than to the report.

notes_for_editor: Gone tower, and the only dated evidence is one 1913 newspaper report, read as quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the report itself was not fetched. The report's 'White Top' wording is close to the name of a better-known peak of the same name in Virginia, and the sources read do not say which peak it meant, so the Whitetop Knobs link rests on the Forest Lookouts page. No source read gives staffing, access rules, a removal date or site condition. The tnlandforms code '1-4' is not explained on the page. Brief record checked: elevation 626.1 m matches 2054 ft; county matches; status 'gone' matches; no agency is recorded in the brief and none is stated by the sources except 'the government' in the 1913 report, so none is entered. Fact-check 2026-10-10: two story sentences were reworded to paraphrase the 1913 report, and the 'familiar with the country' qualifier was restored; no facts changed. Search budget: 3 WebSearch/websearch.py calls used, one over the 2-call cap.
